newsitem.title: POLAND: Polish gov't body approves draft banking law.
newsitem.headline: Polish gov't body approves draft banking law.

text.p: The government economic committee on Monday approved a draft banking law introducing European Union standards into the Polish banking system, the government's press office said in a statement.

Under the draft law, which will be discussed by the full cabinet next year, the presidents of banks operating in Poland would have to be approved by the president of the central bank. Bank board members would have to be vetted by the head of the central bank to be nominated.
The central bank president could also refuse to grant permission to open a bank in Poland if "it would be contrary to the economic interests of the state."
The draft raises the limit of credit concentration for one creditor to 25 percent of the bank's assets, but the threshold can be raised to as much as 50 percent by the central bank president.
The draft also limits the now virtually unlimited options of banks to create companies by restricting a bank's stake in a legal entity to no more than 15 percent of its own assets.

The total sum earmarked for the purchase of securities and real estate cannot exceed 60 percent of a bank's assets, with the exception of other bank shares. The draft facilitates the creation of bank holdings.
Banks will be obliged to keep their liquidity ratio at no less than eight percent of high-risk assets.
